content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper provides a new algorithm to adapting pre-trained denoisers to unseen noise during test time. The proposed method works in two stages. The first stage generates multiple synthetic noisy images that is similar to a given noisy image. This stage primarily works by sampling vectors from a latent space learned using a normalizing flow framework. The second stage involves fine-tuning a denoiser on the synthetic noisy images generated using Noise2Noise framework. The authors wrap this process into a meta learning framework using MAML and shows that this can improve the performance. 

The authors show results by training a network on SIDD dataset and evaluating on 4 different datasets with real noise. They consistently show improvement with their improvement method across datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The paper is tackling an important problem. Test images with unknown distribution is a common problem in denoising, and having a strong method to fix this problem is interesting and of practical importance.

The authors do a good job of explaining the problem well, setting up preliminaries and explaining the experiments. However, I think that the paper might be missing some important baselines/references, and some relevant experimental settings. 

Relevant papers/baselines to be discussed in the paper and put in context of the current work. Test time adaptation of denoisers have received some attention in the past, and I think it maybe good to acknowledge these papers in the work:
1. Section 4.6 of [Soltanayev et. al, NeurIPS 2018](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.01314.pdf). They introduce "unsuerpvised refining", but is limited to use SURE loss function. 
2. [Mohan. et. al. NeurIPS 2021](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2021/file/c7558e9d1f956b016d1fdba7ea132378-Paper.pdf): Introduce a method to adapt pre-trained denoisers to out-of-distribution test image. 
3. [Vaksman. et. al. CVPRW 2020](https://elad.cs.technion.ac.il/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Vaksman_LIDIA_Lightweight_Learned_Image_Denoising_With_Instance_Adaptation_CVPRW_2020_paper.pdf): Their method is extremely similar to what the authors here suggest. They create synthetic noisy images using a denoiser and use those to fine-tune the denoiser and get a better performance. Although they have a much less sophisticated way of generating noisy images since they deal with Gaussian data. 
There are other methods including [Mohan et. al. 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.05478), [Zhang. et. al. 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.07709) that deals with generalization to noise beyond training which may also be of interest. 

I also think that the experiments are missing comparison to some strong single image denoising methods like [Self2Self](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2020/papers/Quan_Self2Self_With_Dropout_Learning_Self-Supervised_Denoising_From_Single_Image_CVPR_2020_paper.pdf) and [Neighbor2Neighbor](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.02824) both of which can generalize and work well on real noise images (I think the papers show results on SIDD as well). 

My other concern with the paper is how convincing the current results are. As I understand, the authors show that the they can adapt from noise in SIDD to the other datasets they consider. However, on looking at the PSNRs of the pre-trained denoiser (without doing any adaptation), they still seem to be doing working well, and the benefit from adaptation seems to be minor. Given this, I believe it might be worthwhile to do some controlled experiments to test how well the method is doing, and what the limits of the methods are. I recommend authors perform experiments with synthetic Gaussian or Poisson noise in datasets, and systematically study how well they can adapt, answering questions like (1) what happens if denoiser h doesn't work as well? (2) when does h work reasonably well? etc. 

Overall I think the idea is interesting, but has to be put in context with the rest of the literature. The experimental section can use some work and be made stronger.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper as written is clear. However, experimental results aren't convincing enough and needs more thorough study. Furthermore, the epxierments lack several strong baselines. No concerns about reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper in the current state may not be ready for publication. However, I think that with some work to put other papers in context, stinger experimental baselines, and more controlled experiments, this could become a nice paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to solve the real-world image denoising problem. The key challenge of this task lies in that the diverse real noise are hard to capture or estimate. To handle the unseen noise, this paper proposes to synthesize the diverse noise with normalizing flow that learns the latent representation of noise. The Gaussian mixture model is adopted to handle the unseen noise. A test-time adaptation is used to further improve the denoising performance. Experimental results demonstrate competitive results on the SIDD Test, SIDD+, Nam and PolyU datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
+ This paper aims to estimate the noise distribution from a group of noisy images with controlled normalizing flow. This idea is pretty straightforward.
+ After getting many different noise distributions, this paper uses GMM to form noisy images that covers a wider range of noise levels.
+ The performance improves with the TPA and FPA strategies

Weakness:
- Noise modeling with conditional normalizing flows has been introduced in Abdelhamed et al. 2019. Please briefly discuss the similarity and difference when mentioning this method.
- In this paper, the author mentioned that "we train the latent space by using multiple distinct normal distributions to learn many different noise distributions". Please explain more about this setup.
- For the "noisy generation performance", the synthetic noise image is conditioned by the camera configurations. How about the other compared methods? Can the author explain more about why the comparison is fair?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: fair good. Some annotations and experimental setups need to be further clafified.

Quality: fair. Here are some minor issues I found in the paper:
- In Algorithm1, the definition of different annotations are not clearly listed. It is not very easy to scroll up several pages and look for what these characters mean. Please consider adding them for better reading experience.
-The title of 3.4.1 should be "... adaptation", there is a typo "adpatation".
- The picture quality of Fig.4 is not very good after zooming in. Consider replacing it with a vector graphics later.

Novelty: good. It can be improved if the author justify the difference with previous works as mentioned in the weakness.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper has some novelty compared to previous works, while it is not clearly illustrated/compared in the paper. To better justify the contribution, the author should consider discussing more about the related works in denoising task(e.g. Abdelhamed et al. 2019, Lee et al. 2020, Li et al. 2021). Besides, this paper needs to be further clarified in descriptions of some methodologies. Thus, I will rate this paper as "marginally below the acceptance threshold". I am also open to change my current rating after reading the other reviewers' comments and the author's feedback.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, authors propose a noisy image generation framework, which first leverages normalizing flow (NF) to simulate noisy images and then uses meta-learning algorithm with N2N loss to train denoising network in self-supervised manner. The contribution and novelty of the paper is limited. The writing and organization of the paper need to be improved.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

1. The approach is simple and easy to understand.
2. The approach is easy to reproduce.

Weakness:

1. The contribution and novelty of the paper is limited. For most component of the paper is referenced to others, the main contribution is the proposed pipeline, which is not novel enough.
2. The writing and organization of the paper needs to be improved, especially the abstract and introduction. It is hard to get the motivation and key problem authors aim to solve. Besides, the captions of the paper need to be clear. For instance, "accuracy" in Table 2 is not well demonstrated, as there is not clear definition of accuracy in image denoising.
3. N2N assumes that the mean of noise is zero, while the real-world noise usually does not satisfy it. Thus, N2N introduces error in the real-world denoising and is not suitable to adopt it. It would be better to give more discussions about it.
4. The experimental part needs to be improved. It is still hard to verify which parts are indeed improved the performance. It would be better to test the effectiveness of the sampling method and meta-learning process by replacing and removing them in the ablation study.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: As demonstrated in the "Strength And Weaknesses", the clarity, quality and novelty of the paper is not well and needs to be improved. Reproducibility is well and easy to reproduce.

The main contribution is above pipeline, while its contribution limited and the effectiveness of the component in the pipeline is not well verified. Besides, the writing and organization of the paper need to be improved too.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed a test-time adaptation method for real-world denoising, which integrates several components, including noisy image generation with the normalizing flow (NF), noise representation modeling in latent space, and (fast) test-time adaptation with meta-learning. The main idea is to first learn an NF to synthesize noisy images, with multi-Gaussian modeling for the noise in the latent space. Then at test time, given a real noisy image, the NF can synthesize noisy images with a similar noise distribution according to the real one, which facilitates the adaptation of the denoising network. Seeking a fast adaptation, the authors also proposed to use a meta-learning strategy, or more specifically, the MAML framework. Experiments on several datasets with real noise have been conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Strength

* The overall framework is reasonable, and the performance seems good.
* The method can generate noisy images given only one single image at the test time.
* The specific modeling of noise within the latent space is interesting

### Weakness

* The authors claimed that they use GMM for noise modeling in latent space. However, according to Line 3 in Algorithm 1, the sampling distribution is indeed a single Gaussian while not a GMM.
* The authors tried several denoising networks to obtain the pseudo clean image. It would be nice to also try using the ground truth clean image, which could provide a performance upper bound for the proposed method.
* The improvement of FPA over TPA seems not very significant (less than 0.1dB on average as shown in Table 1), and therefore it is questionable whether it is necessary to use meta-learning, which is known to make the training more complicated.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
### Clarity

The method is clearly presented and easy to follow.

### Quality

The overall quality of this paper is good, despite the weaknesses mentioned above.

### Novelty

Though the building blocks are mostly existing ones, the authors successfully integrate them all and push a step further for the studied problem, which confirms the novelty of this work.

### Reproducibility

The authors provide many details for implementing their method in both the main text and the supplementary material, and thus I believe it can be accordingly reproduced.
content.summary_of_the_review: Considering the reasonability of the proposed framework, and the promising performance, I would recommend accepting this paper provided the weaknesses mentioned above are well addressed.

content.title: Test-Time Adaptation for Real-World Denoising Networks via Noise-Aware Image Generation
content.abstract: Image denoising aims for a challenging task of recovering clean images from unseen noise, which can follow different distributions depending on scenes, camera models, ISO settings, etc. Previous works have attempted to handle unseen noise by adapting denoising neural networks to each given noisy image. However, a single noisy image can only provide a limited amount of information for training networks. Therefore, we propose to generate noisy images with diverse yet realistic noise that is similar to noise in a given input image. Such noise generation is difficult to achieve given only a single noisy image. To address the challenge, we propose a normalizing flow (NF) framework that can learn the latent representation of noise, conditioned on noisy images. We also employ the Gaussian mixture model to better handle real-world unseen noise by leveraging multiple noise distributions. Using the proposed NF model, our framework can generate multiple synthetic noisy images to facilitate the adaptation of denoising networks to each given image. To further improve the adaptation to unseen noise, we integrate a meta-learning algorithm into our framework. The experimental results demonstrate that our framework substantially improves the performance of several denoising networks on unseen real-world noise across numerous real-world benchmark datasets.
